A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LoSF-UDF, and all supplied pages are readable. v1 includes Appendix A, whereas v2 ends with references and does not include the supplementary material cited for additional reconstructions, robustness tests, and radius/density analyses. These missing materials limit supplementary comparisons.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction scores in Table 2, robustness and denoising experiments, real-scan reconstructions, and additional visual comparisons in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and real-scan results, runtime comparisons, cross-attention ablations, and integrated reconstruction experiments in Tables 2–4 and Figures 7–10.

M1.justification: The original network and supervised loss are retained, but v2 Section 3.3 introduces a substantive integration procedure. Its scheduled objective transfers guidance from the trained LoSF-UDF network to an unsupervised reconstruction loss, with CAP-UDF, LevelSetUDF, and a DEUDF-loss SIREN implementation. v1 mentioned integration without specifying this procedure.

E1.justification: v2 Section 4.5 adds evaluation on 12 detail-rich Threescan models. ShapeNetCars, DeepFashion3D, and real-range scans remain, and both setup sections list ScanNet. The verified addition expands dataset coverage within the existing surface-reconstruction task.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains CAP-UDF, LevelSetUDF, GeoUDF, and DUDF. v2 adds these comparators to the retained real-scan evaluation in Figure 7, where v1 displayed only its own reconstructions. Table 4 additionally compares LoSF with integrated variants, including a self-implemented DEUDF-loss SIREN rather than a standalone published DEUDF baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds normal consistency to evaluation. Figure 5 labels inputs as 48K points, replacing v1's explicit 100K exception for Bunny; this establishes a reported setting revision, not that experiments were rerun. The new integration experiment specifies approximately 20,000 iterations. Existing splits, corruption levels, and DCUDF extraction remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 8 clearly adds two cross-attention ablations, while the denoising ablation is retained. However, v2 refers high-outlier results and radius-bias/point-density analyses to an unavailable supplement. Their relationship to v1's displayed robustness and radius studies cannot be verified, leaving the overall magnitude of this dimension uncertain.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's averages across evaluated models do not introduce run-to-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 broadly replaces scores: clean ShapeNetCars CD changes from 1.085 to 0.611 for LoSF and from 0.568 to 0.773 for DUDF, reversing their reported ranking. v2 specifies L1-CD whereas v1 leaves the variant unspecified, preventing attribution to a same-setting performance gain. v2 also adds normal-consistency, real-scan, timing, ablation, and integration results. Table 4 shows mixed integration effects: CD is 0.409 for LoSF, 0.447/0.429 for CAP-UDF/LevelSetUDF hybrids, and 0.217 for the SIREN hybrid.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the displayed v-saddle definition from z = 1 - h|x| + |y|sign(x)sign(y) to z = 1 - h(|x| + |y|)sign(x)sign(y). These expressions are not algebraically equivalent. The quadratic-surface derivation is otherwise retained, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 briefly claims that initialization can enhance unsupervised methods. v2 makes this more specific, claiming improvements in both reconstruction efficiency and accuracy in the abstract, contribution list, and conclusion. The core claims about shape-independent training and noise/outlier robustness remain.

C2.justification: v2 retains the inability to reconstruct missing parts but adds bias-based radius-selection guidance, a stated density condition of at least 30 points per unit area, and an upsampling suggestion. It also explains integration through the detail-recovery benefits of unsupervised losses. v1's future-work proposal for dynamically adapting the radius is no longer included.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project/code URL, the integration iteration budget and initial 10,000-iteration guidance schedule, and details of the SIREN implementation with PCA-estimated normals. It specifies an i9-13900K/RTX 4090 timing platform and reports RTX 4090-only experiments, whereas v1 listed RTX 4090 and A100 GPUs. v1's per-sample data-preparation timings are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against local reconstruction methods through a dedicated subsection discussing partition-of-unity implicits, LDIF, PatchNets, and adaptive local basis functions. It adds SIREN and DEUDF references supporting integration and removes some traditional-reconstruction discussion, including iPSR and Shape as Points.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and conclusion are revised, related work is reorganized, analysis and ablations receive separate subsections, and acknowledgements are added. Much of the introduction and original method exposition remains closely matched; the scientific additions account for much of the expanded narrative.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the single-column preprint layout with two columns, redraws the architecture diagram, and reorganizes Figure 5's comparison grid. Table 2 gains normal-consistency columns and ranking highlights, while new timing, ablation, and integration displays are added. v1's appendix figures are absent from the supplied v2.

improvement.justification: v2 turns v1's brief initialization proposal into an explicit procedure with measured runtime comparisons, and directly tests the cross-attention design. Its expanded discussion of local reconstruction also improves research positioning. These strengthen the paper's support, although unavailable supplementary analyses and mixed integration accuracy in Table 4 limit the gain. The replaced benchmark scores alone do not establish better paper quality.
